  "reasoning": "All 16 final answers agree with their respective captured Math Academy solutions. However, q-85700 contains an intermediate sign error: its displayed term -(-1)^{2n+1}/(n\\pi^n) equals +1/(n\\pi^n), whereas the required term is negative. Its final answer remains correct. Independently: q-50939 is the exponential series at x=1, giving e. q-85700 uses ln(1-z)=-sum(z^n/n) with z=1/\\pi. De Moivre's theorem multiplies the angles by 20, -5, and -6 in q-104119, q-104343, and q-71452, respectively; cosine is even and sine is odd. For q-82043, multiplying the rotation matrix by (8,-14) gives (-4\\sqrt{3}-7,7\\sqrt{3}-4). For q-170524, cosine is 1/2 and sine is -\\sqrt{3}/2, giving a clockwise rotation through \\pi/3. For q-85637, the trapezoidal sum is (9+2(2)+1)/2=7. Trapezoidal chords lie below concave-down curves and above concave-up curves, confirming the selected graphs for q-49165 and q-49158. The unequal-width trapezoidal sums are 1(1+3)/2+3(3+7)/2=17 for q-116296 and 1(3+5)/2+3(5+7)/2=22 liters for q-116618. For q-51076, the sum is 0.25[3+2(4+3+3)+1]=6 cm. For q-8873, cosine cannot vanish at a solution; tan(x)=-1/2 gives roots -arctan(1/2) and \\pi-arctan(1/2), whose product rounds to -1.24. For q-20701, each half of the even exponential curve has area 1, giving 2. For q-152231, the antiderivative is 2(5^{x/2})/ln(5), whose lower-limit contribution vanishes, giving 2/ln(5). There is no disagreement with any final source answer.",
